newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India rises amid tight supply.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India rises amid tight supply.

text.p: Indian GDRs renewed their recent climb on Wednesday as steady demand and an expected strong run from local stocks in coming days drove gains on thin volumes, traders said.
They said selective demand amid tight supply forced price rises.
"The market believes there will be a run in Indian stocks before the budget (on February 28)," a trader said.
He said SBI, Gujarat Ambuja and Hindalco attracted interest. Hindalco collected $1.12 to $25.87-$26.87 and Gujarat made 65 cents to $8.37-$9.12.
But dealers said current high GDR premiums to local prices were unlikely to hold, and the local market needed a strong run or GDRs could retrace gains.
Traders said the market would be driven by the budget in the next two weeks.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's (BSE) benchmark 30-share index fell 18.79 points, or 0.54 percent, to 3,483.48.
The Indian GDR index closed at 70.19, up 0.93 points or 1.35 percent with the premium over the local market at 17.39 percent from Tuesday's 15.46 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended at 66.12 points, up 0.10 points or 0.16 percent and the premium at 41.43 percent over the local market.
The Taiwan GDR Index closed at 103.73, up 0.67 points or 0.65 percent and a premium of 4.89 percent.
